title: minimize-request-marshalling-and-defer-io-threads
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Reduced CPU-side latency by eliminating per-request copies on the hot path; improved throughput under bursty load; KV cache lookups switched to lockless fast-path for common case; no public API changes.
description: Motivation: We continue to see tail latency spikes on CPU-heavy boxes caused by request marshalling, ephemeral allocations, and the worker-pool being blocked by network IO. This PR attacks the problem on three fronts: 1) Replace per-request serialization copy path with a zero-copy marshalling pipeline that keeps request buffers on the incoming IO arena and hands only lightweight descriptors to CPU workers; 2) Move socket read/write operations off of the worker thread pool to dedicated IO threads with a compact SPSC ring buffer interface, avoiding accidental thread preemption and expensive thread pinning ops on the hot CPU path; 3) Reduce KV cache contention by introducing a fast-path, lockless read using seqlock-style epoch checks, falling back to shared_mutex only on hash-collisions or write cases. Additionally we tweak continuous batching heuristics to pre-reserve batch slots and to prefer same-core batch coalescing when available.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: This looks great; main concern is the lifetime model for arena-backed buffers crossing async boundaries. Can we add a debug-only sanitizer that tracks arena frees?
Leah Park: Added arena debug tracking under build flag ARENA_SANITIZER and a test exercising cross-thread handoff; left comments in request_marshalling.h about ownership semantics.
Tom Becker: The seqlock approach on kv cache is clever, but we need to ensure we don't spin forever under pathological update patterns. Please add a bounded retry and fallback to shared_mutex.
Leah Park: Added bounded retry (8 spins) and immediate fallback and documented the tradeoff. Also added microbench comparing fallback rate.
Riley Chen: CI flake in tests/integration/zero_copy_marshalling_test initially failed on Linux/amd64 with a race. After the fix the integration runs stable locally and on CI.
Tom Becker: Approved after the bounded-retry change and perf numbers look good.
Aisha Khan: Approved — nit: add a small blurb in ops docs about tuning io thread count relative to NIC queues.
